title: Open inference engines adopt a named release-gating security track by H1 2027
body: vLLM's v0.24.0 did not just add throughput: alongside DeepSeek-V4 serving paths and FP8 kernel speedups, it folded a coordinated security-hardening batch into the same release, bumping Starlette past CVE-2026-48710, closing an audio-decompression bomb in the speech-to-text endpoint, and fixing a remote denial-of-service via invalid recovered-token reinjection in speculative decoding. Treating adversarial-input handling, DoS-resistance, and supply-chain patching as release-blocking concerns rather than post-hoc patches is the signature of a serving stack maturing for production multi-tenant exposure, not benchmark demos, and it lands the same week a CVSS 9.5 unauthenticated RCE in an enterprise job scheduler underscores that self-hosted inference and orchestration infrastructure is now an active attack surface. The prediction is that this hardens into a formal maturity axis: by H1 2027 at least two of the major open or self-hosted LLM inference stacks in the vLLM, SGLang, TensorRT-LLM, and TGI class will publish a named, documented security track, a security policy plus coordinated CVE-disclosure process with multi-tenant-exposure hardening (untrusted-input fuzzing on public endpoints, upstream-dependency CVE gating, and DoS-resistance checks) treated as a release-blocking criterion, rather than folding security into general bug-fix churn. Concretely, expect a stated security-response policy, a hardening or fuzzing gate wired into the release checklist, and CVE handling coordinated to a shipped build, so that a serving engine's production-readiness is measured on a security axis the way it is already measured on tokens-per-second. The consequence is that the procurement and deployment bar for standing up self-hosted inference stops being raw performance alone and starts including a demonstrable, versioned security posture, pushing pure-throughput forks and unmaintained engines below the line enterprises will run in a multi-tenant setting.

reasoning.because: vLLM v0.24.0 shipped a CVE, decompression-bomb, and DoS-reinjection batch as release-blocking work.
reasoning.given: Self-hosted inference is a live attack surface, making multi-tenant hardening a production axis.
reasoning.so_that: Major open inference engines publish a named security track with hardening and CVE gating as release-blocking criteria.
reasoning.landing: By H1 2027, two-plus major open inference stacks formalize a security track.
reasoning.plain_language: The software that runs open AI models will start blocking releases on security checks, the way it already blocks on speed.

summary: vLLM's v0.24.0 folded a dependency CVE fix, a decompression-bomb fix, and a speculative-decoding DoS fix into a performance release, treating hardening as release-blocking. Expect two-plus major open inference engines to formalize a named, release-gating security track by H1 2027.
